name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data on how it behaves across different PR types without risking bad outcomes. The trade-off is slower feedback for contributors, but we avoid breaking builds or annoying teams with premature automation. After two weeks, we’ll have hard evidence to decide if it’s worth expanding to all PRs or limiting it to new contributors.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode misses PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It won’t flag real risks, so teams learn to ignore *all* comments—including the ones that matter. Instead, run a controlled A/B test: PR-Agent on 50% of PRs, manual review on the other 50%, then compare error rates and contributor feedback. That settles it with data, not assumptions.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the A/B test on PRs from *new contributors only*—they’re less likely to have strong review habits, so the contrast in error rates will be clearer and the stakes lower. This cuts the sample size needed while still exposing PR-Agent’s false negatives where they matter most.

name: Sprocket
text: Run a 48-hour controlled pilot on PRs from new contributors only. This tests PR-Agent’s false negatives where it matters most—low-trust environments—without risking team-wide disruption. The trade-off is limited data scope, but we avoid drowning contributors in ignored warnings while still exposing real gaps in PR-Agent’s safety checks. If the pilot flags risks we’d miss in shadow mode, we’ll know to refine the model before scaling up.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour controlled pilot on PRs from new contributors only to measure PR-Agent’s false negatives against manual review, with error rates and contributor feedback as the deliverables. Overhaul owns it.
